answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring each node to burn a scarce registration bond like permanent pigment in an unrecoverable sink, paired with trusted enclave hardware attestations. Much like a sparrow bound to its physical body, an identity cannot duplicate its execution context for free; each duplicate imposes a non-refundable capital cost exceeding per-node epoch yield. Draping sybils in a velvet cloak of valid transactions fails because linear burn strictly caps attacker profit.
